{{short description|Soviet physicist}}
'''Nikolai Delaunay, Jr.''' (aka Delone, Nikolai Borisovich; 22 May 1926 – 11 September 2008) was a [[:Category:Soviet physicists|Soviet physicist]] born in [[Leningrad]], [[USSR]] (now [[Saint Petersburg]], [[Russia]]).<ref name=PhysicsToday2009>
{{cite journal
 |author1=Vladimir P. Krainov |author2=Gérard Mainfray |author3=See Leang Chin |author4=Joseph H. Eberly |author5=Pierre Agostini |author6=Mikhail V. Federov |year=2009
 |title=Obituaries: Nikolai Borisovich Delone
 |journal=[[Physics Today]]
 |volume=62 |issue=5 |pages=67
 |bibcode = 2009PhT....62e..67K
 |doi=10.1063/1.3141949 |doi-access=free
}}</ref>

==Life==

Delaunay was born in Leningrad on 22 May 1926. He was the son of [[Boris Delaunay]], a [[mathematician]] known for creating the [[Delaunay triangulation]].<ref name=PhysicsToday2009/> He graduated from the [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] in 1951,  and obtained his PhD at the [[Lebedev Physical Institute]] in the late 1950s.<ref name=PhysicsToday2009/>

Delaunay is recognized for the first observations of [[multiphoton ionization]], in 1965.<ref name=PhysicsToday2009/><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=G.S. Voronov |author2=G.A. Delone |author3=N.B. Delone |author4=O.V. Kudrevatova  |name-list-style=amp |year=1965
 |title=Multiphoton Ionization of the Hydrogen Molecule in the Strong Electric Field of Ruby Laser Emission
 |journal=[[Zh. Eksperim. i Teor. Fiz. Pis'ma v Redaktsiyu]]
 |volume=2 |pages=377
 |bibcode=1965ZhPmR...2..377V
 |bibcode-access=free
 |language=ru
}}<br>
: English translation in {{cite journal
 |author=<!--No need for authors here-->
 |year=1965
 |title=none<!-- No need for title here-->
 |journal=[[JETP Letters]]
 |volume=2 |pages=237
 |doi=
 |bibcode=1965JETPL...2..237V
 |bibcode-access=free
}}</ref> Delaunay, along with Maxim Ammosov and [[Vladimir P. Krainov]], developed the [[ADK formula]], relating [[tunnel ionization|tunneling ionization]] in [[laser field]]s.<ref name=PhysicsToday2009/> He was also a lecturer at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]].<ref name=PhysicsToday2009/> After the [[dissolution of the Soviet Union]], he travelled abroad and worked on international collaborations on multiphoton physics.<ref name=PhysicsToday2009/>

His son was [[Vadim Delaunay]], a poet and dissident, who participated in the [[1968 Red Square demonstration]] of protest against military suppression of the [[Prague Spring]].

==Publications==
Delone published over 200 [[scientific paper]]s, a four-book series on the physics of strong laser fields and on multiphoton physics, and a series of high-school level Russian textbooks.<ref name=PhysicsToday2009/>
